reviewIndependence.decisionRule: Reject when one primary work covers the core mechanism or when the remaining claim is an obvious combination or evaluation protocol; revise only when the evidence chain is insufficient; do not infer novelty from a new dataset, metric, simulator, or juxtaposition of existing modules.

closureStatement.reason: The search found a positive single-work collision in VALINDRA and a reinforcing obvious-combination chain across QoQ, LIMERIC/FABRIC, ETSI CPM/BME, and relevance-aware allocation. Search limitations therefore do not create a revise verdict for the current broad claim.

claimUnderReview.exactNarrowClaim: Value- or semantic-aware CPM selection changes each sender's offered load and the receiver-knowledge state used by other senders; the shared distributed congestion controller therefore creates nontrivial cross-sender feedback. A sender-visible local Jacobian and its spectral radius, estimated before rollout, can predict whether held-out episodes will exhibit persistent oscillation, service starvation, or unfair equilibria.

mechanismElements.element: Receiver-knowledge-aware semantic or VoI selection of CPM objects
Selection changes packet size, offered load, or transmission period
Shared DCC or BME feedback couples every sender to the channel state
Other senders' received information or common congestion state creates off-diagonal cross-sender derivatives
A local Jacobian or equivalent transition matrix yields an eigenvalue or spectral-radius stability boundary

evaluationElements.element: Prospective prediction on held-out episodes rather than post-hoc explanation
Prediction targets include oscillation, starvation, and unfair equilibrium
Controls separate true semantic coupling from a load-matched feedback-off baseline

excludedAsNovelty: using a new driving dataset or traffic trace
adding a new performance metric to an existing controller
placing an existing VoI selector next to an existing LIMERIC, FABRIC, or ETSI controller
estimating the same known local stability condition in a different simulator
reporting held-out accuracy without a new mechanism or theorem

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: VALINDRA is in the same vehicular and Collective Perception domain and contains network-data-aware VoI selection, shared CBR feedback, an all-station coupled transition matrix with off-diagonal entries, eigenvalues, a stability bound, equilibrium, fairness, and starvation handling.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: It does not report the candidate's exact held-out episode classifier or isolate a sender-pair semantic-knowledge Jacobian from common-CBR coupling.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Directly preempts the mechanism-level claim; the remaining difference is an evaluation and system-identification refinement.

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: It provides relevance-aware decentralized channel allocation based on received information and derives a convergence condition and fairness behavior.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: The formal application is broader vehicular messaging rather than an exact ETSI CPM object-selection loop, and no held-out Jacobian classifier was verified.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Reinforces that semantic relevance plus distributed stability is not a new pairing.

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: QoQ is the current direct CPM implementation neighbor: it adapts a VoI threshold using a BME resource signal and explicitly identifies convergence interaction and adaptive CPM period as open work.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: No cross-sender Jacobian, stability theorem, or held-out failure prediction is supplied.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Supplies the modern application loop, but combining it with VALINDRA or standard local stability analysis is an obvious extension unless a qualitatively new dynamical phenomenon is proved.

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: INTERN explicitly studies harmful interaction between separately designed congestion and awareness loops and evaluates an integrated controller for stability, convergence, and fairness.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: It lacks receiver-knowledge-aware semantic CPM utility.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Preempts the generic idea that cross-layer controller coupling itself is the contribution.

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: Congestion-Aware Collective Perception directly maps DCC resources to CPM object filtering and packet size.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: It lacks semantic marginal utility and a coupled spectral analysis.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Preempts content-load coupling as a standalone mechanism.

nearestPriorArt.whyNearest: LIMERIC establishes distributed-rate convergence, fairness, delay/asynchrony stability, and limit-cycle analysis.
nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: No semantic CPM utility is present.
nearestPriorArt.noveltyEffect: Makes local linear or spectral analysis of a DCC controller standard control methodology rather than a new contribution.

nearestPriorArt.remainingDifference: It lacks ETSI shared-channel DCC and stability analysis.

elementByElementComparison.finding: Receiver-knowledge-aware VoI or semantic CPM object selection is directly present in VALINDRA, ETSI CPS rules, and tracking-accuracy-based CPM generation.
CPM content selection already changes object count, packet size, channel duty cycle, off-time, or available BME resource in congestion-aware CP and QoQ.
Distributed CBR or BME feedback coupling all senders is foundational DCC behavior and is explicitly present in VALINDRA and ETSI cross-layer specifications.

VALINDRA's aggregate CBR depends on all stations' selected optional content, and its time-discrete threshold dynamics use an all-station transition matrix with nonzero off-diagonal terms. Network-data-aware VoI also depends on VANET knowledge. The inspected derivation does not separately identify a sender-pair derivative caused only by another sender's semantic knowledge contribution, so that narrower derivative remains unverified rather than wholly absent.

VALINDRA derives the coupled transition matrix, its eigenvalues, and a station-count-dependent local stability condition; LIMERIC and ETSI DCC literature likewise use local linear stability and convergence analysis. Naming the same object a Jacobian or reporting spectral radius does not create mechanism novelty.

No inspected primary source was verified to estimate a local matrix before an episode and then classify unseen semantic-CPM episodes. This is an evaluation-protocol residue, because the governing local stability object and simulator validation pattern are already established.
Oscillation, unfair equilibrium, convergence, and starvation are already explicit vehicular distributed-control analysis targets; only their use as held-out labels differs.
A feedback-off and load-matched control is scientifically necessary to attribute a semantic coupling effect, but experimental controls are not a mechanism contribution by themselves.

noveltyResidue.residue: Estimate a sender-pair-specific local Jacobian for the exact nonlinear QoQ-style BME plus VoI-threshold loop, optionally with adaptive CPM periods and endogenous received-knowledge utility, and test whether its pre-episode spectral radius classifies held-out oscillation, starvation, and unfairness.
noveltyResidue.notFoundExactly: The inspected primary sources did not verify this exact held-out classification protocol or an isolated semantic-knowledge off-diagonal derivative for the 2026 QoQ equations.
noveltyResidue.whyInsufficientForCurrentClaim: VALINDRA already supplies a domain-specific coupled semantic-resource controller, nonzero off-diagonal transition matrix, eigenvalue stability boundary, fair equilibrium, convergence, and starvation analysis. QoQ supplies the modern nonlinear BME-threshold implementation and states the remaining convergence problem. Combining those pieces with standard local linearization and a held-out split is an obvious analysis extension, not a new controller mechanism.
noveltyResidue.possibleNonObviousReframe: A new candidate would need to prove a qualitatively new phenomenon or control law caused by two independently adaptive controllers, delayed endogenous receiver-knowledge state, and asynchronous period changes that cannot occur in VALINDRA's threshold model and is not obtained by applying local linearization to QoQ. That reframe would require a new novelty search and is not a rescue of this candidate.

meaningfulness.conclusion: The engineering problem is meaningful even though the current novelty claim is rejected.

findings.finding: Current ETSI work treats DCC equilibrium, convergence, fairness, and oscillation as deployment-relevant concerns.
The BME exposes a live cross-layer resource signal while leaving application-specific policy open, so poorly designed application adaptation can matter operationally.
QoQ explicitly identifies nonlinear convergence interaction and adaptive CPM period as unfinished research questions in a current value-driven CPM design.
DCC timing can cause measurable oscillation and unfair bandwidth allocation, so predictive diagnostics could still have practical value as engineering tooling.

meaningfulness.boundary: Meaningfulness supports continuing the work as validation, tooling, or standards engineering; it does not establish a novel research mechanism.

feasibilityBoundary.conclusion: A controlled simulator study is feasible, but the evidence does not support claiming that the current synthetic proxy or a simulator port validates the exact real CPM mechanism.

feasibleNow.finding: Artery provides an official open simulation substrate for ETSI ITS-G5 applications and can host CPM and DCC experiments.
VALINDRA publishes explicit controller equations and stability conditions that can be reimplemented as a strong baseline.
QoQ exposes a current concrete adaptive-threshold and BME interaction to reproduce before adding new dynamics.

notEstablished.finding: No official VALINDRA or QoQ codebase was verified in this search, so equation-level reimplementation and independent consistency checks are required.
JigsawComm's official repository did not provide a complete implementation at inspection time, so it cannot yet supply a verified semantic-coupling module.

minimumCredibleExperiment: Reproduce ETSI or LIMERIC, FABRIC, VALINDRA, QoQ fixed-period, and feedback-off load-matched baselines.
Use asynchronous updates, half-step controls, density shifts, communication delays, and heterogeneous utility distributions.
Estimate the local matrix without using the held-out episode outcome and use sender or episode as the statistical unit rather than packets.
Demonstrate a semantic-specific effect that disappears under feedback-off and cannot be explained by aggregate load or synchronized timing.
Treat success as engineering validation unless a new non-reducible mechanism or theorem is established.

preemptionRisks.finding: The same work combines Collective Perception VoI, shared-channel threshold control, cross-station off-diagonal dynamics, eigenvalue stability, fair equilibrium, convergence, and starvation.

preemptionRisks.finding: QoQ supplies the modern adaptive CPM loop, while VALINDRA and LIMERIC supply the local transition-matrix or stability methodology. Applying the latter to the former is foreseeable unless it exposes a new dynamical mechanism.

preemptionRisks.risk: Held-out spectral prediction may be judged as evaluation rather than novelty
preemptionRisks.finding: Transition-matrix eigenvalues, convergence, oscillation, and fairness are established; changing the validation split does not change the mechanism.

preemptionRisks.risk: Semantic cross-agent dependence is independently established
preemptionRisks.finding: Receiver-knowledge-aware CPM selection and cross-agent semantic redundancy are already represented in Tracking Accuracy CPM, VALINDRA, and JigsawComm.

preemptionRisks.risk: Recent 2025-2026 work is rapidly filling metric and object-selection variants
preemptionRisks.finding: Current publications cover accuracy and relevance, uncertainty-aware VoI, path-deviation priority, variable CPM sizes, and semantic-aware radio allocation.

preemptionRisks.risk: AoI-aware decentralized congestion control full text was not inspected
preemptionRisks.finding: The formal title is directly adjacent, but only metadata was verified; no algorithmic overlap is asserted or used for the verdict.

candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.condition: The estimated off-diagonal terms vanish, reverse sign inconsistently, or are fully explained by aggregate load after load matching.
candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.effect: The claimed semantic cross-sender mechanism is unsupported.

candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.condition: Oscillation or unfairness persists unchanged when semantic feedback is disabled, or disappears under a half-step or asynchronous-timing control.
candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.effect: The observed failure is more plausibly classic DCC timing or gain instability than a semantic-coupling phenomenon.

candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.condition: The pre-episode spectral radius does not predict unseen senders, densities, delays, or utility distributions beyond aggregate CBR and controller-gain baselines.
candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.effect: The proposed predictor has no demonstrated incremental validity.

candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.condition: Results are significant only when packets are treated as independent samples but disappear when episode or sender is the unit.
candidateHypothesisFalsifiers.effect: The evidence is pseudoreplicated and cannot support the claim.

verdictReconsiderationConditions.condition: A primary-source reanalysis demonstrates that VALINDRA's matrix contains only common-load coupling and cannot represent any endogenous receiver-knowledge effect, and the new work derives a distinct sender-pair semantic state with a non-reducible stability phenomenon.
verdictReconsiderationConditions.requiredEvidence: A formal state-space distinction, theorem or counterexample, and primary-source comparison against VALINDRA rather than a naming difference.

verdictReconsiderationConditions.condition: The candidate introduces and proves a new two-controller phenomenon caused jointly by adaptive threshold, adaptive period, delayed receiver knowledge, and asynchronous BME feedback that cannot occur in VALINDRA, LIMERIC, or QoQ's current fixed-period setup.
verdictReconsiderationConditions.requiredEvidence: A new mechanism-level result plus experiments that isolate it from classic gain, delay, synchronization, and load effects.

verdictRationale.finding: VALINDRA directly models a value-aware vehicular and Collective Perception resource controller in which all stations' selected content affects shared CBR, threshold dynamics are cross-station coupled through off-diagonal matrix terms, and eigenvalues determine stability, equilibrium, convergence, fairness, and starvation behavior.

QoQ contributes the current adaptive VoI-threshold plus BME loop, while VALINDRA, LIMERIC, FABRIC, and ETSI DCC provide the established stability and fairness machinery. Applying local Jacobian or spectral-radius analysis to the QoQ loop is therefore foreseeable without an additional non-reducible mechanism.

The exact held-out episode prediction protocol and isolated sender-pair semantic derivative were not verified in prior art, but they are evaluation and system-identification refinements of an already modeled coupled controller rather than a new controller principle.

The current candidate must be rejected rather than revised because the core collision is positive and directly verified. A narrower two-controller endogenous-knowledge phenomenon would be a different candidate requiring a fresh novelty closure.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: The search is broad but not a proof of universal absence and did not include an exhaustive patent search.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: Low, because rejection rests on a positive direct collision rather than an absence claim.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: Semantic Scholar was rate-limited with HTTP 429, and only the first ten OpenAlex and Crossref relevance results were screened.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: The failed fan-out could reveal more preempting work but cannot remove the verified VALINDRA collision; no conclusion uses unverified API metadata.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: VALINDRA is a dissertation primary source rather than a single journal article containing every cited derivation, although the related IEEE Access work and current follow-on publication records corroborate the research line.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: The dissertation provides explicit equations and is sufficient primary evidence for technical preemption; venue format does not erase prior disclosure.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: QoQ is a recent arXiv version and may change before formal publication.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: QoQ is used as a current direct neighbor and obvious-combination component, not as the sole preempting source.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: The full text of the AoI-aware DCC conference paper was not verified; only its formal DOI metadata was available in this run.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: No algorithmic claim from that paper is used in the verdict. It remains an unresolved preemption risk.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: No official VALINDRA or QoQ code repository was verified, and JigsawComm's official repository did not expose a complete implementation at inspection time.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: This limits immediate reproduction and feasibility confidence but does not restore novelty to a disclosed mechanism.

evidenceLimitations.limitation: Some publisher full texts were paywalled; formal DOI records were paired with arXiv, author manuscripts, or institutional records where available, and unsupported detail was marked as unverified.
evidenceLimitations.impactOnVerdict: The direct rejection evidence was inspected in full text; paywalled records are corroborating neighbors rather than decisive evidence.
Future work may add further overlap; it cannot retroactively make the already disclosed mechanism novel.
